title: Share bounded coalesced derived-result cache lifecycle and drop redundant retained request payloads
evidence: Both cache full bodies repeat scope generation, represented byte count, access tick, outstanding request, latest pending input, completion acceptance, follow-up scheduling, owner retain/release, minimum-last_used eviction and stats plumbing. Syntax cache 183-264/305-462 parallels projection cache 128-216/258-480.

In-flight source String (syntax) and source_revision (projection) are never read to perform or accept work: only request payload performs it; retained in-flight copies are consulted by accounting. Syntax lookup_missing retains latest + in-flight source and creates worker source clone. Projection displayed_revision remains necessary to pair coherent old display and action source while new revision is pending.
proposal: Use a small private typed cache core for entry lifecycle, keyed request identity, owner release, weights and pruning; keep language normalization and projection old-display policy in their adapters. Store latest source in Arc and in-flight request identity/charge only, without a second payload solely for estimation. Use exact unique request tickets for release/reacquire (do not weaken completion fencing). Avoid a generic async framework or shared cache capacity across unrelated owners.
required_contract_changes: No intended visible behavior change. Preserve syntax plain-while-pending versus projection coherent-old-display distinction, wrap-mode invalidation, every owner/generation fence and each independent count/byte budget. Account worker-retained capacity explicitly rather than deleting its charge.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Approximately 450-550 lines of duplicate lifecycle/admission/release/stat paths replaced by 250-340 lines of typed common core and adapter hooks, after request-identity and focused verification cost. Does not count whole caches as deletions.
estimated_net_lines.overlap: Includes redundant cache payload/accounting cleanup; do not sum another cache/LRU replacement estimate.

verification: Existing cache targets plus release/reacquire same owner/source, ABA completion, inline supersession of outstanding projection, multi-update coalescing, budget rejection and coherent copy-source pairing. Inspect worker ownership before deleting retained payload.

title: Store code-line ranges once and unify the two syntax-span projection loops
evidence: projection.rs 175-199 allocates source-line String then segment String then duplicates identical segment into display_text/raw_text. max_display_text clones another line. All constructions make raw_text equal display_text; exact source_range already exists.

syntax_projection.rs 58-101 and 104-162 duplicate intersection and local UTF-8 span conversion; window path differs principally by initial token binary search/range stop. Consumers in inspected tests pass ordered syntax tokens.
proposal: Represent realized lines as source byte ranges and break metadata over one immutable source handle; materialize only the bounded selected viewport. Use one span projection worker over a token slice selected for the requested source window, with an explicit sorted/nonoverlapping token invariant or robust range indexing. Remove conversion-only source-line/segment vectors and duplicate full/window loops; keep copy-source versus display-source distinction at the owning revision boundary.
required_contract_changes: No product change. Range-backed bounded layout is already required by code-panel spec; this narrow cleanup does not by itself implement the complete target range-backed wrap index. Keep CRLF offsets, empty trailing lines, delimiter-preserving smart-wrap preference and copy reconstruction semantics.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Remove roughly 120-190 lines of duplicated span loop/intermediate string conversion and replace with 40-70 lines of range iteration/accessors plus focused test adaptation. No savings claimed for unimplemented range-backed index.
estimated_net_lines.overlap: Independent of AS-001 cache lifecycle; excludes source revision/accounting work already there.

verification: Existing syntax projection/rendering and transcript_command_preview scenarios; compare UTF-8 ranges and CRLF/empty-line/wrap metadata; verify overlapping/error tokens cannot be skipped by partition_point assumptions; bounded visible allocations and exact copied source.

title: Retain current syntax adapters; Syntect is substantial but not a drop-in simplification
evidence: Full local language bodies reviewed: JSON uses already-resolved jsonc-parser 0.32.4 scanner plus strict parse/key/error overlay; TOML uses taplo 0.14.0 syntax tree; Windows INI is a 111-line deliberately narrow dialect; Markdown tokenizes literal code-panel source. These are not transcript Markdown parsing/reconstruction.

A general scope highlighter could replace substantial adapters only by accepting grammar-derived styling instead of the current strict error/key/delimiter distinctions. Existing resolved parser reuse is preferable when preserving those distinctions; the historical markdown 1.0.0 note refers to removed renderer implementation and is not present resolved-package evidence.
Reusable external investigation retained by the root audit at doc/memory/crates.io/syntect/5.3.0/bounded-code-panel-highlighting.md.
proposal: Keep current parser adapters under current semantics. If Operator chooses general grammar-based code highlighting, prototype Syntect scope-to-Beryl-role mapping with bounded per-line input and admitted persistent parse state; compare it against sharing existing parser token/range utilities before adopting. Do not add Syntect only to replace the small INI scanner or basic Markdown scanner.
required_contract_changes: For broad replacement, approve grammar-based best-effort syntax versus strict JSON/Windows-INI errors and exact role segmentation; preserve source bytes and unknown-label fallback. Define explicit overlong-line syntax-unavailable behavior and bounded parser-state checkpoint ownership. No change approved by this audit.

estimated_net_lines.basis: Retained/inconclusive alternative, not included in savings. Gross local adapters ~1,144 lines; scope mapping, dialect exceptions, grammar assets, errors, line admission and regression verification could erase material savings. No defendable net until fit prototype.
estimated_net_lines.overlap: Would subsume language-specific adapter cleanups, not AS-001 cache ownership.

verification: Read-only evidence only. Candidate would require exact-version Windows and secondary-platform checks with Rust 1.92, grammar output comparisons for all current syntax cases, long-line/regex work limits, cancellation between admitted lines, and source-preserving role output; no install/build performed.

dependency_candidates.features: Proposed default-features=false, features=[parsing,default-syntaxes,regex-fancy]; avoid default-onig C dependency and unnecessary HTML/plist/YAML/default-theme paths. Bundled grammar coverage must be checked, no assumed INI/TOML fit.
dependency_candidates.msrv: No rust-version in release manifest/registry; release CI policy tests stable minus two releases (rolling last-three-stable policy), not fixed 1.92 guarantee.
dependency_candidates.platform: Pure-Rust fancy-regex avoids Oniguruma native linkage. Tagged CI inspected is Ubuntu; Windows support asserted by design portability, not qualified by this audit.
dependency_candidates.maintenance_adoption: Upstream describes mostly complete, maintained/PR-reviewed project; release CI runs bat syntax regressions and fancy engine tests. Typst current manifest consumes syntect 5.3 with regex-fancy; concrete adoption beyond download counts.
dependency_candidates.semantic_limits: parse_line requires one contiguous logical line and returns scope operations; parser state persists across lines, scope stack retained separately. It is not strict syntax validation, provides no Beryl byte/concurrency/CPU budgets, and no GPUI integration. Upstream warns fancy-regex debug performance and feature-specific production exposure differ from default engine.
dependency_candidates.runtime_and_wrapper_cost: Scope mapping and fixed grammar assets plus lazy regex compilation, byte-role translation, bounded checkpoint cache, overlong-line fallback and work scheduling remain Beryl responsibilities. Existing taplo/jsonc-parser may remain for strict validation, eliminating package reduction.
dependency_candidates.advisories: Queried official RustSec advisory-db main recursive tree for crates/syntect and crates/fancy-regex on audit date: no matching direct advisory paths returned. This is not a transitive dependency or clean-bill audit; final resolved feature graph requires review before adoption.
